results.fact: Total elevation gain (gain_ft/itinerary vs approach prose & approach_variant's own gainFt)
results.evidence: The row blends two different approaches: approach, approach_variants, trailhead card and waypoints 1-6 describe the Alpental/Source Lake gully, while itinerary, beta, timing and waypoint 0's note describe Denny Creek via Hemlock Pass. The 9.5 mi / 3,900 ft figure is the published Denny Creek figure for Bryant PLUS Hemlock Peak (Bryant alone is given as 9 mi / 3,600 ft); a separate Denny Creek trip log gives 10.8 mi and 3,521 ft net (2,280 to 5,801 ft). No published source gives a total gain for the Alpental/Source Lake line, so the 3,000-3,400 figure could not be confirmed, and the '9.5-mile round trip' in the Alpental approach prose is the Denny Creek number. Needs a decision on which approach this route carries before any gain/distance number can be made consistent.

overview, high_point_ft and the summit waypoint all give 5,801 ft, but the approach prose and climbing_route step 3 say 5,790 ft. Wikipedia's Bryant Peak article gives 5,801 ft (1,768 m), and a Denny Creek trip log also gives the summit as 5,801 ft.

results.evidence: Waypoint 0 is named Alpental/Snow Lake Trailhead with directions saying ~3,100-3,120 ft, but its elev is 2,300 (the Denny Creek trailhead height) and its note says the Denny Creek/Hemlock Pass approach is the one used; the itinerary and beta are Denny Creek, while approach, variants, trailhead card and waypoints 1-6 are Alpental/Source Lake. The sibling route's '1971' falls inside this row's hedged '1971-72'/'c. 1972'. The only primary record, Don Williamson's note in the 1972 AAJ (party Williamson, Bucher, Oas), gives no ascent date, so the hedge is the honest statement and nothing contradicts it.

results.correct_value: gain_ft 5,140 is right; the summit day (camp to summit and back) is ~3,640 ft, so itinerary day 2 gain/loss and loss_ft change (loss_ft 5,140)
results.evidence: The reader's internal resolution is backwards: camp at Hardscrabble Horse Camp sits at ~2,830-2,860 ft and the summit is 6,540 ft (Wikipedia; Yellowleaf's USGS-quad list), so the summit day must gain at least ~3,650 ft and the itinerary's 2,600 is physically impossible. A 2023 trip report measured 7.5 mi / 1,400 ft from the Dingford gate to Horse Camp and 4.5 mi / 3,822 ft for the summit day from camp. gain_ft 5,140 = 1,400 + 3,640 + 100 matches this, so day 2 becomes 3,640 up/down and loss_ft = 0 + 3,640 + 1,500 = 5,140.
